adjudicator: third pass: claude-opus-5-5 through `claude -p`, no tools, no MCP server, no settings sources, run from an empty directory; given policy-v1 and each disagreement with the two labels in a seeded random A/B order (seed 21083, adjudication-prompt.txt). It was not told which labeller wrote which label, was told to favour neither, and was allowed to answer "unsettled"; it settled every pair.

disagreements.reason: The issue is about where the user lands after a timeout ('doesn't return to login screen', needing 'a bookmark of login screen'). It is a navigation/redirect bug, and nothing in it bears on whether an expired session can be reused.

The defect is that 'user gets no response' because 'login.php never getting called' after logout from an already-expired session. This is a redirect/UX issue, not a question of whether the terminated session stays usable.

The request changes how users authenticate to access the application, via SSO from 'the account or laptop the user used'. Workstation login may be single-factor, and the request does not say whether a second factor is enforced.
disagreements.businessFact: Will the SSO identity provider enforce multi-factor authentication for every user before granting OpenEMR access?

disagreements.reason: The request changes the behaviour of the brute-force lockout counter ('login_fail_counter', 'max reties enabled'). PA-09 defers to the security documentation, and the request does not say what that documentation requires on an admin reset.
disagreements.businessFact: Does the security documentation require the failed-login counter to be cleared when an administrator resets a user's password?

disagreements.reason: The request only removes composition rules ('Do not require passwords to contain numbers, special characters'). It does not touch minimum length, so PA-01 is not engaged. PA-05 is the relevant rule.
'Users may not know that their password have expired' implies expiry exists, but not whether it is periodic rotation or expiry on compromise. Notifications alone do not impose rotation.
disagreements.businessFact: Are passwords configured to expire on a fixed schedule, or only when a password is found to be compromised?

disagreements.reason: The issue is a defect report whose subject is that the CSRF token is 'embedded directly in the URL query string' and leaks via Referer headers, history and logs. Resolving it means removing the token from the URL, which is exactly what DP-01 asks.
The issue flags that the scripts run with '$ignoreAuth = true' but notes they 'historically had to run before any user account exists'. It does not state what access restriction should replace this.
disagreements.businessFact: Must acl_upgrade.php and sql_upgrade.php still run before any user account exists, or can they be restricted to authenticated administrators (or a one-time setup token)?

disagreements.reason: TOTP is added, but requiring it for portal access depends on a 'portal_force_mfa global' toggle. Without the toggle, patients can still log in with username/password alone.
disagreements.businessFact: Will portal_force_mfa be enabled so that every patient must use a second factor to access the portal?

disagreements.reason: The request adds a 'Prescription History' option to the existing Patient Report for a patient chart. It introduces no new object-access path, so object-level authorization is not engaged without a stretch reading.

INSERT/SELECT-only grants and checksum chaining address modification. But protection from unauthorized access is only 'Ideally' achieved by removing the default user's access, and encryption is being removed.
disagreements.businessFact: Will the default openemr database user be denied all access to the log tables, leaving only a dedicated least-privilege account?

consistencyPass.why: Run in #2140, after arms had run on this set (it is a tuning set): adjudication saw only the cells the two labellers disagreed on, so a rule both labellers skipped on a requirement was never checked. governing-03's labels hold the pairs #2140 is about (a blocklist rule on flows that set a password) only because its consistency pass added them, and this set had none. So governing-03's procedure was run here, on the counterparts of its cross-cutting rules: PA-04 (blocklist on registration or change, for PW-07), PA-10 (multi-factor access, for TS-09) and AZ-01 (function-level access, for TS-01). TS-06 (audit) has no single counterpart (this policy splits logging into five narrower rules) and AS-02 (password procedures) none. Two tool-less claude-opus-5-5 sessions per rule were given the policy and all 33 requirements and asked about that one rule alone, on every requirement (labelling/2140/consistency-prompt.txt in id order for pass 1; consistency-prompt-pass2.txt, the same text in a seeded order, seed 21404, for pass 2). They saw no label, no rule summary and no arm.
consistencyPass.decisionRule: A standing label changes only when both blind passes agree on the new label. A cell the passes split on keeps its standing label.

changes.reason: Changes the password policy applied at set/change time but says nothing about checking against a common-password list.
changes.businessFact: Will passwords set or changed under the new policy be rejected if they appear in a list of at least the top 3000 common passwords that meet the policy?

changes.reason: The upgrade scripts are reachable with no authentication at all, but the report gives no fix and notes that they historically had to run before any account exists.
changes.businessFact: Must these upgrade scripts stay reachable before any user account exists, or can they be gated behind authenticated (MFA) admin access?

changes.reason: Adds a new prescription-history report function but is silent on which permission is required to use it.
changes.businessFact: Should the Prescription History report option be available only to users holding an explicit prescription/medication view permission?
